title: 3D Orbital Tracking in a Modified Two-photon Microscope: An Application to the Tracking of Intracellular Vesicles
protocol: Maintain CHOK1 cells in tissue culture flasks using DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 100 I.U/ml of penicillin, 50 μg/ml of streptomycin.
Incubate the cells in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Harvest CHOK1 cells from flasks.
Plate harvested CHOK1 cells on a 14 mm diameter micro-well with a surface thickness of 0.16 mm.
Seed cells to achieve optimal density for imaging, around 60-70% confluency.
Incubate seeded cells overnight at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Wash the cells three times in HBSS (Hank Buffered Saline Solution).
Incubate cells in a solution containing 50 nM of Lysotracker DND-99 green and 150 nM of tubulin tracker green.
Incubate cells for 1 hour at 37 °C.
Wash the cells three times in HBSS to remove any unbound dye.
Add fresh DMEM growth medium prior to imaging the cells.
Align the laser beam in the rear port of the microscope using IR-coated mirrors.
Attenuate the laser beam using a rotating half-wave plate followed by a calcite linear polarizer.
Ensure that the average power at the sample is between 0.5 and 2 mW.
Reflect the laser beam with galvanometer-motor actuated mirrors to control its position in the sample plane.
Expand the collimated laser beam exiting the galvanometer mirrors using a beam expander (10X).
Direct the expanded beam into the rear of the microscope objective after reflection on a short-pass dichroic mirror.
Choose a high numerical aperture water objective (60X, NA 1.2) to collect fluorescence light from the sample.
Select an appropriate fluorescence filter cube based on desired emission wavelengths for either one or two channel configuration.
Use emission bandpass filters to further select the spectral range of emitted fluorescence.
Place the sample onto a motorized stage and adjust its fine motion using an objective piezo-controller.
Direct the light from the filter cube into photomultiplier tubes where the signal is discriminated.
Send the signal from the photomultiplier tubes to a digital I/O data acquisition card.
Position the cells on the stage and focus using transmitted light illumination.
Switch to raster scan imaging to identify cells that have incorporated the dye and visualize underlying microtubules.
Identify the initial area where vesicle movement is present.
Once an isolated vesicle is identified, set the following parameters for orbital tracking:
Select the radius of the orbit to define the size of the circular scan according to the size of the particle being tracked.
For a point emitter, set the radius of the orbit equal to the waist of the Point Spread Function (PSF) of the excitation beam to maximize sensitivity and response.
Set the axial distance to define the distance between the two orbits that are performed to localize the particle position along the axial direction.
Set the axial distance to 1.5-3 times the PSF waist.
Define the dwell time according to the brightness of the particle to set the time spent on each point of the orbit, which will also determine the photo-bleaching rate.
Use a dwell time between 10-100 µsec.
Set the number of points in each orbit to 64 or 128.
Change the DC offset signal through the graphical user interface to center the beam on the particle.
Switch the microscope mode from raster-imaging to orbital scanning.
Activate feedback and data collection.
Use software to display fluorescence collected at each point along the orbit as an ‘intensity carpet’.
Display trajectory information, including DC displacement over time of x,y scanners and z-piezo, and fluorescence intensity collected from photomultiplier tube over time in the form of time series.
Select a region of interest in the trajectory using time series representation and ‘intensity carpet’ information.
Display a 2D projection of the selected portion of the particle trajectory.
Color-code the trajectory according to the particle fluorescence intensity.
Select the option to display the particle trajectory in 3D.
Color-code the trajectory according to the fluorescence intensity.
Rotate the trajectory in 3D using the controls to visualize the features of the lysosome motion along the microtubule.
